featured_reviews.name: Bhavika Mehta-Worah
featured_reviews.review_text:
This has been one of the most disappointing medical experiences I’ve had. We visited this cardiologist for a second opinion, bringing along an angiography CD to assess the percentage of blockage and determine whether angioplasty was necessary or if medication could suffice.

Unfortunately, the doctor was unable to confidently read the CD. Initially, he said he wasn’t sure if there was any blockage at all (raising serious doubts about his expertise as a cardiologist). Then, within just 15 minutes, his diagnosis fluctuated from no blockage, to 30%, to 70%, and finally 70–80%. This inconsistency was alarming and did not inspire confidence.

He began the consultation by noting blood pressure, weight, and other basic vitals. While reviewing the case history and previously prescribed medications, he recommended discontinuing *Cortel-CH* (prescribed by another doctor), claiming it could cause headaches and flush sodium from the body. However, he soon became confused, tore up the initial prescription, and scribbled a new one—this time only listing *Ecosprin Gold-40*, with no other notes or patient details. When asked why he discarded the original, he said it was “messed up,” and that he remembered the measurements, which seemed unprofessional and careless.

Regarding treatment, he first stated that angioplasty wasn’t necessary, then suddenly reversed his stance and strongly recommended it—specifically at Holy Family Hospital in Bandra—while dismissing other reputable hospitals like ACE and Tunga without providing clear reasoning.

Lastly, the consultation fee was ₹4,000, which is fine if the expertise justifies it. But in this case, with so much confusion and lack of clarity, it felt unjustified.

I had chosen him based on reviews mentioning over 15 years of experience, but what we experienced did not reflect that. If you are looking for a reliable, knowledgeable, and confident cardiologist, I would strongly recommend seeking another opinion. Very disappointed with the overall experience.

Thankfully, Dr. Desai and his team had the expertise and experience to carry out this advanced procedure with precision and care. We were also fortunate that the Bandra Holy Family Hospital was equipped with the latest technology necessary for such a delicate operation.

The situation was extremely critical—any minor error could have cost my father his life. Yet, Dr. Desai's team not only managed to place three stents successfully, but also performed the incredibly challenging task of passing the third stent through the first two. Their skill, coordination, and calm under pressure were nothing short of miraculous.

From the bottom of my heart, thank you, Dr. Desai, and your outstanding team. Your dedication and expertise gave my father a second chance at life, and for that, we will always be indebted to you.

Claim denials, partial payments, and delays are common problems with health insurance reimbursement in India, leaving many policyholders financially and mentally stressed. A 2024 survey by LocalCircles found that 43% of policyholders struggled with claims over the previous three years. 
Common reasons for claim rejection

Non-disclosure of pre-existing diseases (PED): This is a leading cause of claim rejection. Failure to accurately disclose medical history when purchasing a policy can lead to denied claims later on.

Waiting period violations: Most health policies have waiting periods for specific diseases, pre-existing conditions, or the initial period after purchase. Filing a claim during this time will lead to rejection.

Incorrect or incomplete information: Providing inaccurate details on claim forms or missing documents is a frequent reason for denial.

Policy exclusions: Claims for treatments or conditions that are specifically excluded from your policy's coverage will be rejected. This can include certain cosmetic procedures, alternative treatments, and specific therapies.

Lapsed policy: If your policy is not renewed on time, any claim filed while it is expired will be rejected.

Exhaustion of sum insured: A claim will be denied if the policy's coverage amount has been fully exhausted by previous claims within the same policy year.

Insufficient hospitalization: If the insurer determines that hospitalization was not medically necessary, the claim may be rejected.

Role of Artificial Intelligence AI in Cardiology.  AI in cardiology enhances patient care by automating image analysis, improving diagnostic accuracy, and predicting risks for conditions like heart failure and arrhythmias. It enables rapid interpretation of ECGs and echocardiograms, often exceeding human efficiency in identifying hidden cardiac issues. Key roles include, but are not limited to: 
Imaging & Diagnosis: AI automates segmentation of cardiac structures, analyzes echocardiograms, and identifies coronary plaque from CT scans faster than manual analysis.
Predictive Analytics: Algorithms analyze large datasets to identify high-risk patients for heart failure rehospitalization, arrhythmias, and stroke, enabling earlier, tailored interventions.
Remote Monitoring & Wearables: AI-driven Apple Watch apps detect low ventricular ejection fraction and irregular rhythms in real-time, aiding early diagnosis of heart disease.
Improved Efficiency: By reducing the time spent on manual data interpretation and EHR documentation, AI allows clinicians to focus on personalized, patient-centered care. 
AI serves as a powerful, non-invasive, and increasingly accurate tool, transforming cardiovascular medicine from reactive to proactive, particularly in detecting subtle abnormalities such as left ventricular dysfunction.

What's Coronary Calcium Score?
A coronary calcium score (or Calcium Score Test) is a non-invasive, CT-scan-based test that measures the amount of calcified plaque in the coronary arteries. By detecting this hardened plaque, it helps estimate the risk of developing coronary artery disease (CAD) and heart attacks, usually for people with intermediate risk factors. 
What the Score Means (Agatston Score)
0: No detectable calcium, indicating very low risk of a heart attack.
1–99: Mild plaque buildup.
100–300: Moderate plaque buildup, indicating high risk of coronary artery disease.
>300: Extensive plaque burden and very high risk of heart attack. 
Key Aspects of the Test
Purpose: Identifies early, silent atherosclerosis before symptoms occur, aiding in decisions regarding lifestyle changes or statin therapy.
Procedure: A quick, painless CT scan of the heart that takes about 10–15 minutes.
Limitations: It measures plaque, not blockages, and does not show non-calcified (soft) plaque.
Radiation: The test involves a small amount of radiation, similar to 23 chest x-rays on average. 
It is primarily used as a predictive tool, not a diagnostic tool for immediate heart blockage.

What is CIMT?
Carotid Intima-Media Thickness (CIMT) measured by ultrasound is a valuable, non-invasive tool for detecting early-stage atherosclerosis, acting as a surrogate marker for systemic vascular disease, including Coronary Artery Disease (CAD). Increased CIMT indicates underlying atherosclerosis, correlating with cardiovascular risk factors, the severity of CAD, and future cardiovascular events, helping to identify individuals at higher risk and guide treatment for better outcomes. 

How CIMT Detects CAD

Early Atherosclerosis Marker: CIMT quantifies the thickening of the inner layers (intima and media) of the carotid artery wall, a sign of subclinical atherosclerosis before symptoms appear.

Correlation with CAD Severity: Studies show a direct relationship: the thicker the CIMT, the more extensive the coronary artery involvement (e.g., single, double, or triple-vessel disease).

Risk Stratification: High CIMT, along with plaque presence, helps identify patients with increased risk for heart attack, stroke, and other cardiovascular events, refining risk assessment beyond traditional factors. 

What CIMT Measures

Measurement: It's the distance between the first bright line (lumen-intima) and the second bright line (media-adventitia) on high-resolution ultrasound of the common carotid artery.

Normal vs. Elevated: Values typically range from ~0.5 to ~0.9 mm, but increase with age, with higher values suggesting more disease.

Leadless pacemaker is a tiny, self-contained capsule—roughly 90% smaller than traditional devices—implanted directly into the heart to treat slow heart rates without wires (leads) or a chest pocket. It offers a minimally invasive, catheter-based solution with fewer long-term complications, such as infections or lead failures. 

Key Advantages of Leadless Pacemakers:

No Leads or Surgical Pocket: By eliminating wires, it removes risks of lead fracture, dislodgement, and associated infections. There is no, under-the-skin, "pocket" or incision in the chest.

Minimally Invasive Procedure: Inserted via a catheter through the femoral vein (leg), resulting in a faster procedure, minimal scarring, and quicker recovery.

Cosmetic and Physical Comfort: The device is invisible, causing no, under-the-skin, lump on the chest. Patients feel no physical discomfort while moving.

Fewer Activity Restrictions: Due to the absence of wire, patients often face fewer restrictions on upper body movement after the initial healing period.

MRI Compatibility: These devices are designed to be safe for use in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) machines.

Long-Lasting: The device has a long battery life, typically lasting 10–15 years. 

Leadless pacemakers are particularly beneficial for patients with high infection risks, vascular issues (e.g., dialysis patients), or prior device-related complications.

Dr. Kahale is not just an outstanding cardiologist — he is compassionate, ethical, deeply knowledgeable, and incredibly reassuring for both patient and family. In a time filled with anxiety and difficult decisions, he gave us confidence, clarity, and hope.

I was asked to redo the medical test on my own expenditure and confirm to my client if Iam fit for the company.

I happened to call many cardiologists and was lucky enough to get in touch with Dr. BRIJESH AGRAWAL - Cardiologist, Interventional Cardiologist.
Thanks to Ms. Sonal from the receptionist who helped me with  booking the appointment on the spot and solved all my queries. I asked her many questions with respect to the tests done, experience of the doctor, fees etc. I found her professional, smart and quick which made me very comfortable.
Dr. Brijesh Agrawal heart clinic is in Chembur above Malhar Hotel. It was crowded with patients but we were taken inside at the right time slot. inshort, we didn't have to wait for hours like I did in my previous health checkup experience.
Dr. Agrawal is a very knowledgeable and down to earth person.  He is 40+ years old and an interventional cardiologist with more than 15 to 20 years of experience in cardiology, but looks like a teenager :)

He saw all my old reports (2 days old report which shows blockage) and asked me to do a 2D EchoCardiography and Tread mill test.
With the blessings of God, Iam perfectly alright and the previous report turned out to be wrong.
Dr. Brijesh Agrawal explained in detail about Heart functions, how 2D  EchoCardiography would be carried out and I was in total ease before entering the 2D room.
The room was very neat and clean and the equipment looked to be of latest make. I was asked to lay on one side and then a colourless gel was applied to the chest area. Then Dr. Agrawal moved the transducer across the various parts of his chest to get specific/desired views of the heart.
I was happy to see that he was doing it personally and was not dependent on any technician to do it for him.

After 2D Echo I was asked to do Treadmill test wherein I was asked to walk on a treadmill for say 5 minutes.
Before getting onto the treadmill Ms. Sonal and Sister Shivani briefed me how tests would be done and asked me to change the shirt so that the small, flat, sticky white patch can be put on the chest and then electrodes / wire were attached to them. They'll be attached to an electrocardiogram monitor -- called an EKG - that charts your heart's electrical activity during the test.

Within 15 minutes of both the tests being done, I again met Dr. Agrawal with the reports where he declared me fit and fine.  He gave me a fitness certificate which I shall be submitting to my new company !
I was very happy with the service and appreciated the time he gave me and my mother. He explained the entire process of Heart function and was always smiling.

Once again thank you very much Dr. Brijesh Agrwal. I Am very thankful for a quick check up and detailed explanation.

P.s - Incase someone is looking for a good Gynecologist, then I would also suggest to check with Dr. Pradnya Supe who sits in the same clinic.

Regards,
Anuj Saini

When Is Mechanical Circulatory Support Recommended?

Mechanical Circulatory Support (MCS) is an advanced treatment option used for patients with severe heart failure when the heart is unable to pump enough blood to meet the body's needs. These specialised devices help support heart function and improve blood circulation, especially in patients with advanced cardiac conditions.

MCS may be recommended for individuals experiencing severe heart failure symptoms despite medication and standard treatments. It can be used as a temporary support during recovery, as a bridge to a heart transplant, or as a long-term treatment option for selected patients. The goal is to improve blood flow, reduce symptoms, and enhance quality of life.

Patients with persistent shortness of breath, extreme fatigue, swelling in the legs, or worsening heart function may require evaluation by an experienced cardiac surgeon in Mumbai. In advanced cases, mechanical circulatory support may also be used while awaiting treatment from a qualified Heart Transplant Surgeon in Mumbai

Early diagnosis and timely intervention are important in managing complex heart conditions. Modern cardiac care offers advanced technologies that help support patients with severe heart disease and provide better treatment outcomes.

If you or a loved one has been diagnosed with advanced heart failure, consulting a specialised cardiac team can help determine the most appropriate treatment approach.

Early Warning Signs of Aortic Dissection

Aortic dissection is a serious and life-threatening condition where there is a tear in the inner layer of the aorta, the main blood vessel carrying blood from the heart. Early recognition of symptoms is critical for timely treatment.

🔹 Common Warning Signs
• Sudden, severe chest or upper back pain (often described as tearing)
• Pain that spreads to the neck, jaw, or abdomen
• Shortness of breath
• Weakness or loss of consciousness
• Difficulty speaking or stroke-like symptoms

🔹 Who is at Higher Risk?
• People with high blood pressure
• Individuals with heart or connective tissue disorders
• Older adults
• Those with a family history of aortic disease

🔹 Why Immediate Care is Important
Aortic dissection requires urgent medical attention. Delaying treatment can lead to serious complications. Quick diagnosis and expert care can save lives.

Consulting an experienced cardiac surgeon in Thane/Mumbai is essential for proper evaluation and treatment. Access to advanced care from the best cardiac surgeon in Thane/Mumbai ensures better outcomes and patient safety.

Timely medical attention and awareness of symptoms can make a life-saving difference.

Who Needs a Ventricular Assist Device (VAD)?

A ventricular assist device (VAD) is a mechanical pump that helps the heart circulate blood when it is not able to function properly. It is commonly used in patients with severe heart failure to support heart function and improve quality of life.

A VAD may be recommended in the following situations:

• Advanced Heart Failure: When the heart is too weak to pump enough blood to the body
• Waiting for Heart Transplant: Used as a temporary support while waiting for a donor heart
• Not Eligible for Transplant: Helps improve heart function in patients who cannot undergo a transplant
• Severe Symptoms: Such as breathlessness, fatigue, and reduced ability to perform daily activities
• Poor Response to Medication: When medicines alone are not effective in managing heart failure

VADs can significantly improve blood circulation, reduce symptoms, and help patients lead a more active life under proper medical care.

If you or your loved one is experiencing symptoms of advanced heart failure, early consultation is important. A qualified cardiac surgeon in Thane / Mumbai can evaluate your condition and guide you toward the most suitable treatment options.

When Is Aortic Surgery Necessary?

The aorta is the main artery that carries oxygen-rich blood from the heart to the rest of the body. If the aorta becomes weak, enlarged, or damaged, it may lead to serious health complications. In such cases, doctors may recommend aortic surgery to prevent life-threatening conditions and protect heart health.

Aortic surgery may be required in the following situations:

• Aortic Aneurysm: When a portion of the aorta becomes enlarged due to a weakened wall. If it grows larger, there is a risk of rupture.
• Aortic Dissection: A tear in the inner layer of the aorta that can cause severe chest or back pain and requires urgent medical attention.
• Severe Aortic Valve Disease: When problems with the aortic valve affect normal blood flow from the heart.
• Genetic Conditions: Certain inherited conditions may weaken the aorta and increase the risk of complications.
• Chest Trauma: Serious injury from accidents can sometimes damage the aorta.

Early diagnosis and regular heart check-ups help detect aortic conditions before complications develop. Symptoms such as sudden chest pain, back pain, breathlessness, or dizziness should not be ignored.

Consult the Best cardiac surgeon in Thane/ Mumbai for expert evaluation and advanced treatment options to maintain better heart health and safety. ❤️

When Should You Consider Heart Valve Surgery?
Heart valves play a vital role in maintaining healthy blood flow through the heart. When these valves become damaged, narrowed, or start leaking, they can affect overall heart function and daily life. In such cases, heart valve surgery may be recommended to restore proper circulation and prevent serious health complications.
Common signs of valve problems include shortness of breath, chest pain, fatigue, dizziness, swelling in the legs, and irregular heartbeat. Ignoring these symptoms may lead to worsening heart conditions over time. Consulting an experienced cardiac surgeon in Thane/Mumbai helps in early diagnosis and timely treatment.
Advanced diagnostic tests such as echocardiography and cardiac imaging allow doctors to evaluate valve function accurately. Based on the results, the specialist may suggest medication, regular monitoring, or surgical intervention when needed. Guidance from the best cardiac surgeon in Thane/Mumbai ensures that patients receive personalized care with modern treatment techniques.
After surgery, proper rehabilitation, lifestyle changes, and follow-up care play an important role in recovery. With expert support and timely medical attention, most patients can return to an active and healthy life.
If you experience persistent heart-related symptoms, early consultation can make a meaningful difference in long-term heart health.
